frequency_question: How often do secondary sanctions on major foreign banks occur within a 4-year window of establishing major energy embargoes?
membership_rule: Includes cases where a major superpower issues comprehensive energy embargoes and subsequently faces non-compliance from large trade partners whose major commercial banks process transactions for the target state. Excludes minor secondary warnings without bank-level asset freezes or SWIFT cutoffs.
window: 4-year duration corresponding to the presidential/regulatory term structure

cases.name: US Iran Sanctions (CISADA / NDAA implementation phase)
US Russia Sectoral Sanctions (Post-Crimea enforcement phase)
US Iran Maximum Pressure (SWIFT and bank disconnection phase)
US Russia Comprehensive Sanctions (Post-Ukraine escalation phase against major third-party banks)

coverage_note: 4 named; population covers the entirety of modern unipolar/multipolar secondary sanction enforcement history
known_gaps: Historical precedent is limited by the modern evolution of SWIFT-based extraterritorial financial warfare.
skeleton: Enumerate major sanction regimes with extraterritorial enforcement components since 2000
multiplier: 4 major escalation cycles identified across different geopolitical contexts
validity_reason: Based on structural great-power competition dynamics and international payment architecture which evolves over multi-decade horizons.
